subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: Should OpenClaw reclaim live current-PID session locks beyond startup cleanup, and what liveness signal makes that safe for transcript integrity?
rationale: Current main can clean a narrow untracked self-owned lock shape, but the remaining reports involve live or recovery-created locks where deleting solely because the PID matches the gateway could race a legitimate writer.

options.title: Add holder liveness before reclaim
options.body: Use a heartbeat or active-run ownership signal before treating live current-PID locks as stale, then cover startup, recovery, acquisition, doctor, and status visibility.

options.title: Narrow to startup cleanup
options.body: Declare the startup sweep sufficient for this issue and track runtime/recovery-created same-PID locks in a separate canonical report.

options.title: Keep manual recovery only
options.body: Preserve live current-PID locks by default and rely on doctor/status guidance for operator-driven cleanup until stronger proof arrives.

recommendation.title: Add holder liveness before reclaim
recommendation.body: Use a heartbeat or active-run ownership signal before treating live current-PID locks as stale, then cover startup, recovery, acquisition, doctor, and status visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source blame and recent session/gateway hardening history make this the strongest routing candidate for the reclaim policy decision.
